citations.quote: Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.
The forced incompressible Newtonian branch adopts $$\operatorname{div}u=0,\qquad \rho_0\bigl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u\bigr)=\rho_0b+\operatorname{div}\sigma.$$
When separately selected, no-slip is the stronger adopted equality $u=w_b$ on the wall.

Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be a bounded open time interval measured in seconds and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a fixed bounded open spatial domain measured in metres whose boundary is locally a Lipschitz graph after rigid coordinate changes. Take $\rho_0>0$ kilograms per cubic metre and $\mu_0>0$ pascal seconds as primitive branch-local physical parameters: this forced branch adopts them as constant density and dynamic shear viscosity inputs and derives neither from another framework nor from observations. Let $u:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ be a twice continuously differentiable velocity in metres per second, $p:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R$ a once continuously differentiable pressure multiplier in pascals, and $b:I\times\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ a continuous body-acceleration field in metres per second squared. Define $D=(\nabla u+\nabla u^{\mathsf T})/2$ and the stress tensor $\sigma=-pI_3+2\mu_0D$ in pascals, where $I_3$ is the $3\times3$ identity and $(\operatorname{div}\sigma)_i=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}\sigma_{ij}$.

The forced incompressible Newtonian branch adopts

$$\operatorname{div}u=0,\qquad \rho_0\bigl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u\bigr)=\rho_0b+\operatorname{div}\sigma.$$

Equivalently, since $\mu_0$ is constant and $\operatorname{div}u=0$, its momentum equation is

$$\rho_0\bigl(\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u\bigr)+\nabla p=\mu_0\Delta u+\rho_0b.$$

The derived kinematic viscosity is $\nu_{\mathrm{phys}}=\mu_0/\rho_0$ in square metres per second. Pressure is a constraint multiplier, not an equation-of-state pressure. When the stationary no-slip branch is selected, additionally require that $u$ admit a continuous extension $\overline u:I\times\overline\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ of its interior values, and define its classical wall trace by $u_\Gamma(t,x):=\overline u(t,x)$ for $(t,x)\in I\times\partial\Omega$. This extension, when it exists, is unique because $\Omega$ is dense in $\overline\Omega$. The separately selected no-slip boundary datum is $u_\Gamma=0$; the extension requirement is additional boundary regularity, and neither it, this equality, nor the body force follows from the interior balance. This is a forced branch of the Newtonian model: it adds the prescribed acceleration field to the unforced branch and makes no claim of solution existence or empirical validity.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $d\in\{2,3\}$, let $D\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected Lipschitz polygonal or polyhedral open set, let $T>0$ and $\nu>0$, and let $\mathcal T_h$ be a conforming shape-regular affine simplicial mesh of $D$. Let $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_N=T$ be a finite time partition with $\tau_n=t_n-t_{n-1}>0$, and put $h=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}\operatorname{diam}(K)$ and $\tau_{\max}=\max_n\tau_n$.

Write $V=H^1_0(D;\mathbb R^d)$, $Q=L^2_0(D)=\{q\in L^2(D):\int_Dq=0\}$, and $V_\sigma=\{v\in V:\operatorname{div}v=0\}$. Let $S^1_h$ be the continuous piecewise-affine scalar space on $\mathcal T_h$. For each simplex $K$ with barycentric coordinates $\lambda_{K,0},\ldots,\lambda_{K,d}$, set $b_K=(d+1)^{d+1}\prod_{j=0}^d\lambda_{K,j}$ on $K$ and extend $b_K$ by zero outside $K$. The conforming MINI spaces are
$$V_h=[S^1_h\cap H^1_0(D)]^d\oplus\bigoplus_{K\in\mathcal T_h}b_K\mathbb R^d,\qquad Q_h=S^1_h\cap Q,$$
and their weak divergence kernel is $Z_h=\{v_h\in V_h:b(v_h,q_h)=0\text{ for every }q_h\in Q_h\}$. Let $P_{Z_h}$ denote the $L^2(D)^d$-orthogonal projection onto this finite-dimensional subspace.

For $v,w\in V$, set $\varepsilon(v)=(\nabla v+\nabla v^{\mathsf T})/2$, $a_\nu(v,w)=2\nu\int_D\varepsilon(v):\varepsilon(w)\,dx$, and $b(v,q)=-\int_Dq\,\operatorname{div}v\,dx$. For $a,v,w\in V$, use the real skew convective form
$$c(a;v,w)=\frac12\int_D\big((a\cdot\nabla)v\cdot w-(a\cdot\nabla)w\cdot v\big)\,dx.$$
Thus $c(a;v,w)=-c(a;w,v)$ and $c(a;v,v)=0$.

A smooth MINI interface consists of a forcing $f\in L^2(0,T;L^2(D)^d)$, an exact no-slip velocity-pressure pair $(u,p)$, and a mixed backward Euler MINI solution $(u_h^n,p_h^n)_{n=0}^N$ with the following conditions. The exact pair has $u\in W^{1,\infty}(0,T;H^2(D)^d\cap V_\sigma)$, $p\in W^{1,\infty}(0,T;H^1(D)\cap Q)$, and satisfies
$$(\partial_tu(t),v)_{L^2}+a_\nu(u(t),v)+c(u(t);u(t),v)+b(v,p(t))=(f(t),v)_{L^2},\qquad b(u(t),q)=0$$
for every $v\in V$, $q\in Q$, and almost every $t\in(0,T)$. The continuous representatives of $u$ and $p$ are used at the time nodes, and $u_0=u(0)$. The discrete initial value is $u_h^0=P_{Z_h}u_0$. With $f_h^n=\tau_n^{-1}\int_{t_{n-1}}^{t_n}f(t)\,dt$, each $u_h^n\in V_h$ and $p_h^n\in Q_h$ satisfies
$$\left(\frac{u_h^n-u_h^{n-1}}{\tau_n},v_h\right)_{L^2}+a_\nu(u_h^n,v_h)+c(u_h^n;u_h^n,v_h)+b(v_h,p_h^n)=(f_h^n,v_h)_{L^2},\qquad b(u_h^n,q_h)=0$$
for every $v_h\in V_h$, $q_h\in Q_h$, and $1\le n\le N$.

For a family of bounded real-linear velocity sensors $\ell_n\in V^*$, define the endpoint-sampled exact and discrete observations by
$$\mathcal O(\ell;u)=\sum_{n=1}^N\tau_n\ell_n(u(t_n)),\qquad \mathcal O_h(\ell;u_h)=\sum_{n=1}^N\tau_n\ell_n(u_h^n).$$
Define the accumulated exact and discrete pressures by $P(t)=\int_0^tp(s)\,ds\in Q$ and $P_h^0=0$, $P_h^m=\sum_{n=1}^m\tau_np_h^n$. Let $\bar p_h(t)=p_h^n$ on $(t_{n-1},t_n]$. For $\xi\in Q$ and $\eta\in C_c^\infty(0,T)$, define the accumulated-pressure observation $(P(t_m)-P_h^m,\xi)_{L^2}$ and the time-tested pressure observation $\left(\int_0^T(p(t)-\bar p_h(t))\eta(t)\,dt,\xi\right)_{L^2}$. The latter is an integrated pressure functional; it is not a pointwise-in-time pressure value. This definition supplies inputs and observables only and asserts no error rate or solver-existence result.

The conforming MINI spaces are $$V_h=[S^1_h\cap H^1_0(D)]^d\oplus\bigoplus_{K\in\mathcal T_h}b_K\mathbb R^d,\qquad Q_h=S^1_h\cap Q,$$ and their weak divergence kernel is $Z_h=\{v_h\in V_h:b(v_h,q_h)=0\text{ for every }q_h\in Q_h\}$.
Then the endpoint-sampled observations of the interface satisfy $$\left|\mathcal O_h(\ell;u_h)-\mathcal O(\ell;u)\right|\le \nu^{-1/2}C_*H\,\|\ell\|_{\ell^2_\tau(V^*)}.$$

Under $x=\ell_0y$, $t_{\mathrm{phys}}=(\ell_0/U_0)t^*$, $u_{\mathrm{phys}}=U_0u^*$, $p_{\mathrm{phys}}=\rho_0U_0^2p^*$, and $b_{\mathrm{phys}}=(U_0^2/\ell_0)f^*$, the distributional time-derivative, convection, pressure-gradient, viscous, and body-force terms have common acceleration scale $U_0^2/\ell_0$ after division by $\rho_0$; the dimensionless viscous coefficient is $\nu^*=\mu_0/(\rho_0U_0\ell_0)$. The zero physical wall trace remains zero after division by $U_0$. The strain and skew-convection identities in the Statement show that the resulting equation is exactly the continuous weak equation in the MINI interface. This scaling uses the adopted distributional equation and does not infer classical $C^2/C^1$ regularity from the Sobolev hypotheses.
